notes: READ IN FULL 20 September 2026 (evening) from the author's PDF, v2.1, 47 pages. The notes after the marker EARLIER NOTES were written from the ResearchGate version note and stand where they do not conflict with this. CONTENTS. Theorem 3.3: explicit bijection Phi : U(d) -> J(d+1), V -> (V, 1, 0^m) with m = floor(lambda(d+1) - |V|), hence X(d+1) = W(d) for d >= 1 (Remark 3.4: fails at d = 0). Remark 3.5 concedes the counting content is Winkler's column-sum identity and Barbera's construction, that X(d) = A100982(d) with values back to Wagon and Roosendaal (order 1000, 2005), and that the length count W(k) is A076227. Theorem 5.2 (2-adic rigidity): for equal length and equal weight, nu_2(Q_k(v) - Q_k(w)) = j_min - 1, the first differing index; Remark 5.6 derives it from the Terras-Lagarias correspondence. Theorem 6.3: log_2 W(d) = gamma d + O(log d), gamma = lambda H(1/lambda) = 1.505644, c = lambda - gamma = 0.079319, by Proposition 6.2 (cycle-lemma bounds C(k,d)/k <= W(k,d) <= C(k-1,d-1), the irrationality of lambda making the partial sums pairwise distinct, Lemma 6.1) and entropy bounds; Remark 6.4 the KL form. Remark 6.5, THE LENGTH-BASIS ANALOGUE: log_2 W(k) = H(1/lambda) k + O(log k), so rho_k = 2^(-(1 - H(1/lambda)) k + O(log k)) with 1 - H(1/lambda) = 0.050044 -- Lagarias's eta, proved independently and without citing Theorem D. Remark 6.6 says that to the best of the author's knowledge no asymptotic formula for either sequence had appeared in the literature; Theorem D of Lagarias 1985 is that formula, and the paper cites Lagarias 1985 only for injectivity. Section 7: Table 1 N(k) to k = 10^4, Table 2 W(d) and rho_d to d = 10^4 (extending the A100982 b-file to order 2218), Table 3 the residual Delta_d = log_2 W(d) - gamma d against -(3/2) log_2 d at d = 100, 1000, 5000, 10000, stated to lie in a band of width under 0.3 bits over 100 <= d <= 10000 while Delta_d itself moves 10 bits. Conjecture 7.1: W(d) = Theta(d^(-3/2) 2^(gamma d)), 'numerical in nature and not used elsewhere in this paper', with the rho_d form carrying the trivial factor 2^(frac(lambda d) - 1). THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS FOR PAPER B, Section 7.3, after Table 3: the remaining bounded fluctuation is 'plausibly governed by the fractional part {lambda d}, which determines the terminal distance to the critical boundary'. That is the phase of Paper B's prefactor, named as a plausibility in one sentence, with no function of the phase, no measurement of the dependence, no statement that the prefactor fails to converge, and no mechanism. Paper B's Section 6 quotes it since the 20 September evening edition and claims novelty for the function, its measurement and the barrier-step mechanism only. VERIFIED HERE: all four rows of Table 3 recompute exactly, to the printed three decimals, from the laboratory's survivor counts, W(d) being the minimal-certificate count 2N_(k-1) - N_k at the first-crossing length k of weight d+1 (tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_hikawa_tables.py). AND HIS BAND IS WRONG AS PRINTED: over every d in 100 <= d <= 10000 the difference Delta_d + (3/2) log_2 d runs from -0.046 to 0.472 on the exact counts, a 0.518-bit band, against the 'width less than 0.3 bits' of Section 7.3; his four tabulated rows span 0.236 bits, which is where the sentence must come from. That 0.518 is the laboratory's own earlier measurement (J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic), now settled against his text rather than his version note: his tolerance cannot see the oscillation, and his own range contains it. Acknowledgments: the author used Anthropic's Claude for English grammar and LaTeX. References worth the laboratory's attention: Hercher 2023 (no Collatz m-cycles with m <= 91; registered as hercher-2023-collatz-m-cycles), Barina 2025 (3x+1 verified to 2^71; registered 2026-09-20 as barina-2025-collatz-verification-limit), Barbera 2025 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16886068, residue classes and stopping time), Winkler arXiv:1709.03385 v7 of February 2026. The September paper, hikawa-2026-finite-parity-vector-structures, is this paper's revision under a new DOI: it drops Remark 6.6, Remark 6.5 and the {lambda d} sentence, and keeps only the terminal distance, as Open Problem 1. EARLIER NOTES (version note only, 19-20 September): docs/problems/juggler_jump_spectrum.md. FULL TEXT NOT READ -- ResearchGate returns 403 to fetching and its PDF link opens a save dialog rather than rendering. What is recorded here is the author-written version note on the ResearchGate record itself, v2 of July 2026 and v2.1 of 2 August 2026, read in the browser pane. PROVED, Section 6: log_2 W(d) = gamma d + O(log d) with gamma = lambda H(1/lambda) about 1.5056, lambda = log_2 3 and H the binary entropy function, so the normalized relative density decays at the explicit rate c = lambda(1 - H(1/lambda)) about 0.0793 bits per unit weight, in the information-theoretic form c = lambda D(1/lambda, 1/2); by a cycle-lemma argument plus standard entropy estimates, with a length-basis analogue also given. That rate is the length-basis eta of lagarias-1985-3x+1-problem divided by beta: eta/beta = 0.0793185. CONJECTURED, Section 7, Conjecture 7.1: W(d) = Theta(d^(-3/2) 2^(gamma d)), because over 100 <= d <= 10000 the residual log_2 W(d) - gamma d agrees with the ballot-type correction -(3/2) log_2 d to within 0.3 bits. THIS IS THE PRIOR STATEMENT OF THE d^(-3/2). It is a Theta, in the weight basis, numerically motivated and not proved, and its 0.3-bit tolerance is wide enough to absorb a bounded oscillating prefactor without seeing one. No oscillation, no almost-periodicity, no amplitude constant. The September 2026 revision, Finite Parity-Vector Structures in the Accelerated Collatz Map, doi 10.13140/RG.2.2.24486.28480, carries the same Section 6 result and states outright that the sequence values are not claimed as new.
